items.title: 8.2.2 Some Deductions from the binomial expansion of (a + x)^n (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 155-156: 8.2.2 Some Deductions from the binomial expansion of (a + x)^n, deductions (i)-(iv), sum of coefficients 2^n, odd/even coefficient sums, Example 14

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum binomial theorem se kuch "deductions" nikaalenge. Deduction ka matlab hai ek bare formula se nikalne wale chhote chhote natije (results). Tareeqa bohat seedha hai: formula (A) har \(a\) aur \(x\) ke liye sach hai, to hum \(a\) aur \(x\) ki jagah aasan values (jaise 1 ya \(-1\)) rakh kar dekhenge ke kya milta hai. Yeh results exercise ke "show that" wale sawalon mein bohat kaam aate hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: (A) ek identity hai, yani \(a\) aur \(x\) ki har value par sach. Isi liye hum is mein koi bhi khaas value rakh sakte hain. Hamari taraf se misaal: \((a + x)^{2} = a^{2} + 2ax + x^{2}\) mein \(a = 1, x = 1\) rakhein to \(4 = 1 + 2 + 1\); sahi! Har nayi value ek naya natija deti hai. Neeche chaar aisi values istemal hongi.

(i) (A) mein \(a = 1\) rakhne se:
\[(1 + x)^{n} = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1}x + \binom{n}{2}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[+ \binom{n}{r}x^{r} + \dots + \binom{n}{n-1}x^{n-1}\]
\[+ \binom{n}{n}x^{n} \quad \text{(B)}\]
\[= 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^{2} + \dots\]
\[+ \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}x^{r}\]
\[+ \dots + nx^{n-1} + x^{n}\]
Kyun: \(a = 1\) rakhne se \(a\) ki har power \(1\) ban jati hai (\(1^{n} = 1\)), is liye sirf coefficients aur \(x\) ki powers bachti hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Deductions (i), (ii), (iii) aur (iv) mein kitab "in (I)" likhti hai, jab ke jis expansion ki baat ho rahi hai us ka label (A) hai. Is page par har "(I)" ko (A) parhiye. Humne upar seedha (A) likha hai.

Doosri shakal is liye sahi hai kyun ke
\[\because\ \binom{n}{r} = \dfrac{n!}{r!\,(n-r)!}\]
\[= \dfrac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)(n-r)!}{r!\,(n-r)!}\]
\[= \dfrac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\((n-r)!\) kat kyun jata hai? \(n! = n(n-1)(n-2)\cdots 1\). Is product ko \(r\) factors ke baad, yani \((n - r + 1)\) par rok dein; jo bacha, \((n-r)(n-r-1)\cdots 1\), woh bilkul \((n-r)!\) hai, jo neeche wale \((n-r)!\) se kat jata hai.
Aasan alfaaz mein: \(\binom{n}{r}\) = "\(n\) se neeche ki taraf \(r\) factors, phir \(r!\) se divide". Misal: \(\binom{7}{3} = \dfrac{7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5}{3!} = \dfrac{210}{6} = 35\).
Yeh doosri shakal 8.3 mein bohat zaroori hogi, jahan \(n\) negative ya fraction bhi ho sakta hai aur factorial wali shakal kaam nahin karti.

(ii) (A) mein \(a = 1\) rakh kar aur \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) likh kar:
\[(1 - x)^{n} = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1}(-x) + \binom{n}{2}(-x)^{2}\]
\[+ \binom{n}{3}(-x)^{3} + \dots + \binom{n}{n-1}(-x)^{n-1}\]
\[+ \binom{n}{n}(-x)^{n}\]
\[= \binom{n}{0} - \binom{n}{1}x + \binom{n}{2}x^{2} - \binom{n}{3}x^{3} + \dots\]
\[+ (-1)^{n-1}\binom{n}{n-1}x^{n-1}\]
\[+ (-1)^{n}\binom{n}{n}x^{n} \quad \text{(C)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\((1 - x)^{n}\) mein \(x\) ki odd power wali terms negative aur even power wali positive hoti hain, kyun ke \((-x)^{r} = (-1)^{r}x^{r}\), aur \((-1)\) ki even power \(+1\) aur odd power \(-1\) hoti hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \((1 - x)^{3} = 1 - 3x + 3x^{2} - x^{3}\). Signs \(+, -, +, -\) baari baari.

(iii) Binomial coefficients ka jor (sum) nikaalne ke liye (A) mein \(a = 1\) aur \(x = 1\) rakhte hain. Yani
\[(1 + 1)^{n} = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots\]
\[+ \binom{n}{n-1} + \binom{n}{n}\]
ya
\[2^{n} = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots\]
\[+ \binom{n}{n-1} + \binom{n}{n}\]
Lihaza binomial expansion ke tamam coefficients ka jor \(2^{n}\) hota hai.
Kyun: \(x = 1\) rakhne se \(x\) ki har power bhi 1 ban jati hai, aur sirf coefficients jama hote reh jate hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(n = 4\) par check kijiye: \(1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 16 = 2^{4}\).
Ginti wala matlab (yeh samajh aa jaye to formula kabhi nahin bhoolega): \(n\) cheezon ke set ke kul subsets kitne hain? Ek tareeqa: 0 cheezein chuno, 1 chuno, ..., sab \(n\) chuno; kul \(\binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \dots + \binom{n}{n}\). Doosra tareeqa: har cheez ke liye do faisle, "andar" ya "bahar", to kul \(2 \times 2 \times \dots \times 2 = 2^{n}\). Dono jawab barabar hone chahiyein, aur yahi deduction (iii) hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal: 3 dost (A, B, C) hon to picnic group banane ke tareeqe (koi na jaye se le kar sab jayein tak) \(1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8 = 2^{3}\).

(iv) (A) mein \(a = 1\) aur \(x = -1\) rakhne se:
\[(1 - 1)^{n} = \binom{n}{0} - \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} - \binom{n}{3} + \dots\]
\[+ (-1)^{n-1}\binom{n}{n-1} + (-1)^{n}\binom{n}{n}\]
Is liye
\[\binom{n}{0} - \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} - \binom{n}{3} + \dots\]
\[+ (-1)^{n-1}\binom{n}{n-1} + (-1)^{n}\binom{n}{n} = 0\]
Kyun: left side \((1 - 1)^{n} = 0^{n} = 0\) hai (har positive \(n\) ke liye).

Agar \(n\) odd positive integer ho, to plus wali terms ek taraf aur minus wali doosri taraf le jane se
\[\binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots + \binom{n}{n-1}\]
\[= \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{3} + \dots + \binom{n}{n}\]
Agar \(n\) even positive integer ho, to
\[\binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots + \binom{n}{n}\]
\[= \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{3} + \dots + \binom{n}{n-1}\]
(odd \(n\) par aakhri coefficient \(\binom{n}{n}\) minus wala hota hai, is liye woh right side par jata hai; even \(n\) par woh plus wala hai, is liye left side par rehta hai.)
Lihaza binomial expansion ke odd coefficients ka jor us ke even coefficients ke jor ke barabar hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan "odd coefficients" se murad odd jagahon (1st, 3rd, 5th, ...) wale coefficients hain, yani \(\binom{n}{0}, \binom{n}{2}, \binom{n}{4}, \dots\); aur "even coefficients" se even jagahon wale, \(\binom{n}{1}, \binom{n}{3}, \dots\). Alternating sum mein pehle group par \(+\) aur doosre par \(-\) hai; kul zero hai, to dono group barabar.
Ek qadam aage: dono milkar \(2^{n}\) bante hain (deduction iii), aur dono barabar hain, to har group ka jor \(2^{n-1}\) hai. \(n = 5\) par check: \(1 + 10 + 5 = 16\) aur \(5 + 10 + 1 = 16 = 2^{4}\).
Khud sochiye: \(n = 6\) par \(\binom{6}{0} + \binom{6}{2} + \binom{6}{4} + \binom{6}{6}\) kitna hai? (Jawab: \(1 + 15 + 15 + 1 = 32 = 2^{5}\).)

Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain jis mein yahi deductions ek "show that" sawal hal karti hain. "Show that" sawal mein jawab pehle se diya hota hai; aap ka kaam left side se shuru kar ke, har qadam ki wajah ke saath, right side tak pohanchna hai. Right side ko dekh kar andaza lagaiye ke kaun sa formula kaam aayega.

blocks.title: Example 14
steps:
Given: jor \(\binom{n}{1} + 2\binom{n}{2} + 3\binom{n}{3} + \dots + n\binom{n}{n}\).
To prove: yeh \(n \cdot 2^{n-1}\) ke barabar hai.
Method: right side mein \(2^{n-1}\) dekh kar foran khayal aana chahiye ke kahin na kahin deduction (iii) lagegi, lekin index \(n - 1\) ke saath. Plan: har \(\binom{n}{r}\) ko product form \(\frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}\) mein likhenge, aage wale multiplier \(r\) ko \(r!\) se kaatenge, \(n\) common lenge, aur bracket ko \((1 + x)^{n-1}\) ke coefficients ka jor pehchaanenge.

Step 1: Terms ko product form mein likhein
\[\binom{n}{1} + 2\binom{n}{2} + 3\binom{n}{3} + \dots + n\binom{n}{n}\]
\[= n + 2\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!} + 3\dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}\]
\[+ \dots + n \cdot 1\]
Kyun: \(\binom{n}{1} = n\), \(\binom{n}{2} = \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}\), \(\binom{n}{3} = \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}\), aur \(\binom{n}{n} = 1\). Product form mein aage wala number \(r\) aur neeche wala \(r!\) aamne saamne aa jate hain, jo kaatne ke liye zaroori hai.

Step 2: Kaatein aur \(n\) common lein
\[= n\left[1 + (n-1) + \dfrac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2!} + \dots + 1\right]\]
Kyun: \(\frac{2}{2!} = 1\) aur \(\frac{3}{3!} = \frac{1}{2!}\); aam taur par \(\frac{r}{r!} = \frac{r}{r \cdot (r-1)!} = \frac{1}{(r-1)!}\). Har term mein \(n\) ka factor hai, is liye use bahar nikaal diya.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{r}{r!}\) ko \(\frac{1}{r}\) likhna aam ghalti hai; \(r!\) mein se sirf ek \(r\) katta hai.

Step 3: Bracket ko pehchaanein
\[= n\left[\binom{n-1}{0} + \binom{n-1}{1} + \binom{n-1}{2} + \dots + \binom{n-1}{n-1}\right]\]
Kyun: \(1 = \binom{n-1}{0}\), \(n - 1 = \binom{n-1}{1}\), \(\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2!} = \binom{n-1}{2}\), ..., aur aakhri 1 \(= \binom{n-1}{n-1}\). Yeh index \(n - 1\) ke tamam binomial coefficients hain; yani bracket ke andar ab \(n\) ki jagah \(n - 1\) wala pattern chal raha hai.

Step 4: Deduction (iii) lagayein
\[= n \cdot 2^{n-1}\]
Kyun: index \(m\) ke tamam binomial coefficients ka jor \(2^{m}\) hai; yahan \(m = n - 1\).

Tasdeeq:
\(n = 3\): left side \(\binom{3}{1} + 2\binom{3}{2} + 3\binom{3}{3} = 3 + 6 + 3 = 12\); right side \(3 \cdot 2^{2} = 12\).
\(n = 4\): \(4 + 2(6) + 3(4) + 4(1) = 32 = 4 \cdot 2^{3}\). (Computer se \(n = 1\) se \(8\) tak bhi check kiya gaya.)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Example 14 ka chhupa hua formula yeh hai: \(r\binom{n}{r} = n\binom{n-1}{r-1}\). Misal: \(3\binom{5}{3} = 3 \times 10 = 30\), aur \(5\binom{4}{2} = 5 \times 6 = 30\). Barabar! Yeh identity yaad rahe to Example 14 ek line ka sawal ban jata hai: har term \(n\binom{n-1}{r-1}\) hai, aur un sab ka jor \(n \cdot 2^{n-1}\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(a = 1\): \((1 + x)^{n} = \sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom{n}{r}x^{r}\), aur \(\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)}{r!}\).
2. \(a = 1\), \(x \to -x\): \((1 - x)^{n}\) mein signs baari baari badalte hain.
3. \(\binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \dots + \binom{n}{n} = 2^{n}\).
4. \(\binom{n}{0} - \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} - \dots = 0\); odd jagahon aur even jagahon ke coefficients ke jor barabar, har ek \(2^{n-1}\).
5. Kaam ki identity: \(r\binom{n}{r} = n\binom{n-1}{r-1}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Coefficients ka jor \(2^{n}\) ki jagah \(2n\) likh dena.
2. Alternating sum minus se shuru karna: yeh \(+\binom{n}{0}\) se shuru hota hai.
3. Example 14 mein \(r\) ko \(r!\) se ghalat kaatna: \(\frac{r}{r!} = \frac{1}{(r-1)!}\), \(\frac{1}{r}\) nahin.
4. Example 14 mein bracket ko \(2^{n}\) samajh lena; bracket index \(n - 1\) ka hai, is liye \(2^{n-1}\).
